en: The Paramārthadharmavijaya Sūtra, translated by the Brahmin Gautama Prajñāruci of the Northern Wei:
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Bhagavat was staying in the city of Gayā, not long after having attained enlightenment.

He was accompanied by the most eminent among the eminent bhikṣus, a multitude of ninety-nine billion bodhisattvas, as well as twenty-eight billion devas, eighty-six thousand bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās, and sixty thousand mallas.

There were twelve hundred million followers of the Nirgranthas and eighty-four thousand seers possessing the five supernatural powers—some scorching their bodies with five fires until they were emaciated and fleshless, possessing only skin and bone, with the skin of their bellies adhering to their spines; their hair matted like felt, their bodies bent and hunched, wearing garments of deerskin or tree bark, and holding water-jars in their hands—all arrived at the place where the Buddha was, desiring to engage in strife and contention.

At that time, the World-Honored One’s radiance was preeminent, his majestic and sublime form surpassing all sages. He was like Mount Sumeru, the king of mountains, rising from amidst the Black Mountains; like a six-tusked elephant king among a flock of sheep; like the sun and moon made manifest by the glow of fireflies; like a mandārava flower among fragrant blossoms;
and like the Garuḍa king among flocks of birds—possessing a twofold majesty. The Buddha among the sages was likewise so.
At that time, the World-Honored One entered the Śrī-vimokṣa-samādhi and manifested immeasurable and innumerable supernatural powers;
from his left and right sides, he emitted immeasurable rays of light, producing the bodies of immeasurable billions of Tathāgatas,
the bodies of immeasurable billions of Bodhisattvas, and the bodies of immeasurable billions of Śakra-devānām-indras and Mahābrahmās.
The World-Honored Lord further produced immeasurable hundreds of thousands of arhats;
he further produced immeasurable thousands of bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās;
and he further produced immeasurable universal monarchs (cakravartin), powerful wheel-turning kings, minor wheel-turning kings, and Han-polin.
Those from Nāga and Devīra, people from the southern lands, those who have attained spells from rishis, people from remote border regions,
kṣatriyas of great lineage, as well as brahmins, householders, lay devotees, humans, non-humans, and others—
all such beings with names, adorned with various and diverse forms.
Even the hosts of devas all emerged from the body of the Tathāgata.
At that time, the great assembly was filled with doubt and looked at one another.
All the bodhisattvas within that great assembly were filled with joy; they rained down various jewels, even raining down all manner of adornments everywhere.

At that time, the World-Honored One arose from the *śarabha-vikrīḍita-ratna-samādhi* (the Samādhi of the Lion’s Playful Display of Jewels) and, with a lion’s springing gait, surveyed the ten directions. As he surveyed them, his vision pervaded the ten directions, reaching as far as the range of the Buddha-eye.
The Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, in all the Buddha-worlds of the ten directions—all those Buddhas observe the Sahā world as if looking at the palm of their hand.

All those Buddhas manifest supernatural powers without any difference from what the World-Honored One Śākyamuni has manifested; the emanations produced from the bodies of all those Tathāgatas, down to every single detail, are likewise exactly so, and they arrive at the assembly of the World-Honored One Śākyamuni.
Having arrived there, they all entered the great assembly of the World-Honored One.

At that time, immeasurable bodhisattvas in this assembly, together with bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River, all offered unspeakably many articles of worship to the World-Honored One.
Having made these offerings, they remained close to the Tathāgata.

In this same manner, the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and others, having witnessed the miraculous feats of the World-Honored One, all came to where the Buddha was.
At that time, the bodhisattvas who had come from the ten directions made unsurpassed offerings to the World-Honored One.
Having completed their offerings, they sat upon seats where the six pāramitās had been fully realized.
In this manner, even humans, non-humans, and others sat upon seats corresponding to their own respective appearances.
The emanations of the World-Honored One extended upward as far as the celestial palaces of the Akaniṣṭha heaven and downward as far as the Avīci hell.

Furthermore, having arrived at the site of the Avīci Hell, everything emanated from the bodies of those Buddhas of the ten directions all entered into every pore of Śākyamuni; and everything emanated from the body of the World-Honored One Śākyamuni there all entered into the bodies of the Buddhas of the ten directions.

At that time, there was a bodhisattva mahāsattva in the assembly named Vijitaskandha. He rose from his seat, adjusted his robes over one shoulder, knelt with his right knee on the ground, and with palms joined toward the Buddha, praised him in verse, saying:
“O Lord of Men!
"How most rare! Quickly show this to all the worlds; never before has such a thing existed.
The hosts of Māra have vanished and do not appear; looking at one another, they say:
'This matter is most rare.'"
For what reason have I come here?
It is for the purpose of destruction.
I, who was once a seer, am no longer a seer now; my body is emaciated, nothing but skin and bone.
The aged and withered possess no joy; they have not attained these supernormal powers.
Though he manifests supernormal powers, he does not speak of them, for he removes the thorns from the Buddha-dharma.
The disciples of the Buddha rejoice at dawn; the Venerable One acts as the Lord of the Buddha-dharma.
Sentient beings conceived a sense of the rare and marvelous, their minds pure and filled with joy.
All the hosts of devas said:
"May we attain Buddhahood."
O Lord of Men!
Within this assembly, the disciples of immeasurable Buddhas dwell; Mañjuśrī leads them, and they follow him here to this gathering.
This Mañjuśrī has already made offerings to many Buddhas;
now, before this great assembly, the Buddha manifests various kinds of supernatural powers.
What is the nature of this dharma?
"What does the Muni intend to do?
This assembly has doubts; we pray that out of compassion for sentient beings, you will speak.
At that time, by means of his majestic spiritual power, the Tathāgata caused a great seer within the assembly, named Prabhāketu, to address the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vijitaskandha:
"The youth remains silent, the youth remains silent.
Now that I have posed this difficult question, if you can explain it so as to be purified yourself, you may rightly be called one who corresponds to omniscience."

If it were the illusory transformations produced by Nārāyaṇa or Maheśvara through the *tāpīra* mantra, such a feat would not be extraordinary; for such illusory transformations can be accomplished by ordinary people, and need not necessarily be the work of a Buddha.
At that time, the World-Honored One smiled serenely.
Having observed the assembly of sages, he addressed the Great Sage Jyotirasa, saying:
"O Life-Sustaining Great Sage!
"You should pose questions; according to your capacity, I am able to purify [your doubts].
At that time, the Great Seer Jyotirasa said:
"I shall question Gautama, and Gautama shall explain each point to me."
From where are all sentient beings born? What are sentient beings?
By what causes and conditions is the kalpa consumed by fire at its end?
From what place did sentient beings come together in the past to be born among humans?

By what signs can one know that within the bodies of sentient beings there is a subtle inner self (adhyātman), measuring one cubit, or two cubits, or two finger-breadths, or one finger-breadth; is it like a large barley grain, or like a small wheat grain, or should it be like a bean, or like sesame, or like a mustard seed?
At that time, the World-Honored One praised the great seer Jyotirasa, saying:
"Excellent, great seer! Excellent, excellent!"
“You, Great Seer, have constantly practiced for a lifespan of sixty kalpas; it is now that you ask such questions with these marks.
Among the assembly of seers, another great seer thought to himself:
“I have always lived in the forest, yet I was neither aware nor knew of the lifespan of this Great Seer Jyotirasa.”
"No one has yet explained how the śramaṇa Gautama came to know this.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the great seer Prabhāketu, saying:
"Great Seer, listen attentively and reflect well upon it; I shall now explain it for you."

Regarding your question as to where all sentient beings are born: this principle is without words and without speech; rather, through the sequential conditions of ignorance, up to birth, old age, death, and so forth, sentient beings are born.
Furthermore, O Great Seer!
Sentient beings arise from causes and conditions; that is to say, they are born through the causes and conditions of their parents.
Furthermore, O Great Seer!
The union of father and mother is the cause for sentient beings;
that is to say, after passing through kalpas, one is impelled by the winds of karma and falls into the female organ—this is the causal condition.
Furthermore, O Great Sage!

That which is subsumed under the Noble Truth of Suffering, the Noble Truth of the Origin of Suffering, the Noble Truth of the Cessation of Suffering, and the Noble Truth of the Path Leading to the Cessation of Suffering is called a "sentient being.
Furthermore, the five aggregates of clinging (*pañcopādānaskandha*) and the eighteen elements (*aṣṭādaśadhātu*), etc., are called sentient beings.
Great Seer, you should know:
those truths, aggregates, and elements are themselves sentient beings and are not different from karma;
likewise, karma is not different from sentient beings.
"Great Seer, you should know:
sentient beings do not decrease, and sentient beings do not increase.
At that time, the Great Seer asked:

“Gautama! If sentient beings neither decrease nor increase, why is it that some sentient beings exercise mastery as gods or humans, yet later become dogs, and then again become gods or humans who exercise mastery?”
The Buddha said:
"Great Seer! As you have stated, this meaning is not so."
If there were sovereignty, it would not be dependent on another.
Thus, O Great Sage!
If the body were sovereign, how could it later become non-sovereign?
Great Seer, you should know this:
it is as if a firefly were to give rise to such a thought:
‘This light of mine can completely and universally illuminate the entire Jambudvīpa.’
"The light emitted by those fireflies has no causal conditions that could enable it to universally illuminate the entire Jambudvīpa.
In this same way, all untrained minds lack true sovereignty."
Furthermore, O Great Seer!
If the one who is sovereign has diminished afflictions while the dog has many afflictions, then the dog is sovereign.
Thus, that which is not sovereign becomes sovereign; therefore, sovereignty is also non-sovereignty.
"If the dog were self-mastering and equal to afflictions, then sentient beings would neither decrease nor increase.
The Great Seer said, "Gautama, do you not sever afflictions?"
The Buddha said, “Great Seer!
You do not understand afflictions; I have understood afflictions, yet I do not sever afflictions.”
The Great Seer said, "If it is so, then you possess mastery.
The Buddha said:
"Great Seer! It is so, it is so. Because they are unreal, I am sovereign."
The Great Seer said: “Gautama! Let this matter rest; let it be set aside.”

If, as the son of Gautama previously stated, sentient beings are born from the union of father and mother, then since many sentient beings frequently engage in sexual union and experience much sensual pleasure, there ought to be few who are actually born.
"What is the meaning of this?
The Buddha said, "Great Seer!"
I shall now question you with a simile.

Suppose there is a single seed that produces a single tree; from that one seed and one tree, immeasurable fruits are produced. Among those immeasurable fruits, some are capable of serving as seeds, while others are not.
"What more is there to say about this? He replied, "Gautama!"
"Due to the conditions of the wind, the seeds of the tree have been scattered and lost.
The Buddha said, "Great Seer!"
The fruits of all sentient beings are likewise; they are scattered by the winds of karma.
Great Seer, you should know:
some are devoured by worms while still within the womb, while others are dispersed and destroyed by the winds of karma.
Great Seer, you should know this:
trees and the like have few obstructions, whereas sentient beings have many hindrances.
Furthermore, Great Seer!
The realms of all sentient beings arise from conceptual discrimination.
Great Sage, you should know that the minds and mental factors of all sentient beings function and circulate everywhere, and all possess objects of perception; this meaning has already been explained.
"In this way, Great Seer!
The realms of all sentient beings arise from conceptual discrimination.
Having heard this, the Great Seer spoke as follows:
“Just so, just so; Gautama has already cleared away this difficult question.
Furthermore, Gautama, you should further explain what the meaning of the kalpa-conflagration is.”
The Buddha said:
"Great Seer! Because it is impermanent, I thus teach that the dharma-realm is consumed by the kalpa-fire."
Great Seer, you should know this:
if the earth were to be consumed by the fires at the end of the kalpa, then the dharma-realm would be dual—thus there would be both the permanent and the impermanent.
If such were the case, all Tathāgatas would be speaking untruths.
"Furthermore, Great Seer!
If all phenomena are entirely impermanent, subject to change, and unstable, then the Tathāgata is rightly named the Omniscient One.
Having heard this, the Great Seer spoke thus to the māṇava:
"This name is the name of omniscience corresponding to reality as it is.
The Buddha said, "Great Seer!"

If the Tathāgata were not to release the conflagration at the end of the kalpa, all sentient beings would not know the passage of time, nor recognize the name of the kalpa, nor recognize the time of conflict, nor recognize the time of peace.
Great Seer, you should know this:

if the Tathāgata were not to release the conflagration at the end of the kalpa, there would be no one at all who could perceive the differences in the karmic retributions of wholesome and unwholesome deeds.
Furthermore, Great Seer!
It should be known that this is the Tathāgata’s skillful means for releasing the conflagration at the end of the kalpa.
Great Seer, you should know:
because all sentient beings believe in the conflagration at the end of the kalpa and fear being burned by it, they all gather merit and virtue and place their faith in the Tathāgata.
"Furthermore, Great Seer!
It is like a python named Sāhuka; that Sāhuka python can summon with its eyes, it can summon with its ears, it can summon with its nose, and it can summon with its mouth."
In this way, Great Seer!
The Tathāgata is likewise; he gathers [beings] through generosity, and through kind words, beneficial actions, and cooperation.
Furthermore, Great Seer!

For example, it is as if someone places gold in fire; it is not out of anger toward the gold that it is placed in the fire, but rather to ensure it is well-refined so that it may correspond with its true nature as a treasure. If it corresponds with its true nature as a treasure, then it becomes of great value.
Great Seer, you should know:
by these causes and conditions, it is beaten until it is thoroughly refined and pure.
Thus it is, Great Seer!
"The Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, do not release the kalpa-ending conflagration without cause and condition, nor are there sentient beings who are burned by the kalpa-fire.
At that time, the Great Seer Jyotirarcis said:
"How extraordinary, World-Honored One!"
"I shall release the fires of the kalpa-conflagration, yet not a single sentient being shall be burned by those kalpa-fires.
The Buddha said, "Great Seer!"
Not a single sentient being has been burned by the Tathāgata.
Furthermore, Great Seer!
It is as if a fine rain were to fall throughout the ten directions; the number of Tathāgatas is even greater than that.
The Bodhisattvas of the ten stages are likewise; they abide upon it.
Having thus taken their place, they all use their own hands to rescue sentient beings and cause them to attain liberation.
Great Seer, you should know:

when such beings see the physical forms and colors of the Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas as being dignified and majestic, and having seen this, further see the great fires at the end of the kalpa consuming everything and then see themselves liberated, they give rise to joy and a pure mind, making this aspiration:
"May I also deliver all sentient beings in this way; may my physical form and color also be dignified and majestic like theirs; may my body also become golden in color."
Once sentient beings have given rise to such thoughts, some attain liberation of mind and immediately realize arhatship;
some, seeing the kalpa-fire, give rise to revulsion and detachment, while others realize the stage of srotāpanna,
some realize the stage of sakṛdāgāmin, some realize the stage of anāgāmin, and some realize...
Among those who are arhats, some have realized the path of the pratyekabuddhas; some have realized the patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena (anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti);
some have attained the stage of non-retrogression; some have attained birth in the realm of the Four Great Kings;
some have attained birth in the Heaven of the Thirty-three; and some have attained birth in the Yāma Heaven. Or...
Some attained rebirth in the Tuṣita Heaven; some attained rebirth in the Nirmāṇarati Heaven;
some were born in the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven; some were born among the Brahmakāyika, Brahmapurohita, and Brahmakāyika devas;
and so on in succession up to those born in the Akaniṣṭha Heaven.
In this way, there are those who become universal monarchs (cakravartin), powerful wheel-turning kings,
or minor kings of India; likewise, O Great Sage,
even up to kṣatriyas, brāhmaṇas, or householders (gṛhapati).
Great Seer, you should know:
by this expedient means, having caused them to see the marks of the Tathāgata’s form-body, they will perceive their own bodies and give rise to great fear.
Having attained liberation, they will recognize the kindness of the Tathāgata, repay the Tathāgata’s kindness, draw near to the Tathāgata, and listen to the True Dharma.
Having heard the Dharma, they practice and train according to the Dharma with heedfulness; by these means, they cause all sentient beings not to enter the evil realms.
Furthermore, O Great Sage!

Even as far as the range of vision of Bodhisattvas of the ten stages, and all the realms of earth therein—far exceeding these realms of sentient beings—all those sentient beings perceive the faults of birth and death and enter the realm of nirvana without remainder.
"Great Seer, you should know:
by this cause and condition, the kalpa is set ablaze and utterly consumed.
At that time, the Great Seer named Jyotirhṛdaya (Light-Torch-Mind) immediately reflected:
"This son of the Śākyas—a Great Man endowed with the six pāramitās, a supreme person—does not call me by my name, but addresses me as 'Great Sage'."
"I have personally tested whether I am omniscient or not;
I now truly know that I am omniscient, and I should now declare my name according to reality."
At that time, the Great Seer named Jyotirarcis, having finished his reflection, addressed the Buddha, saying:
"O Mass of Great Merit, Possessor of Immeasurable Wisdom!"
"O Omniscient One! Please explain to me further where those sentient beings come together.
The Buddha said:
“Great Seer! You should know that the non-reunion of sentient beings is reunion; you should know that the equal reunion of sentient beings is reunion;
you should know that the reunion of sentient beings in the One Vehicle is reunion.”
All are in harmony with bodhisattvas, meaning they abide within the realm of nirvana without remainder.
Great Seer, you should know that sentient beings are thus harmonized in a placeless state.
"Great Seer, you should know this:
just as various small rivers and great rivers, once they have entered the great ocean, all become of one single taste;
even so, Great Seer!"
When all sentient beings have exhausted their outflows (*āsrava*), they all experience the flavor of liberation; all are equal, and the Bodhisattvas are in harmony.
"Furthermore, O Great Sage!
If sentient beings are brought together within the ocean of birth and death, I say that their union is not true harmony.
Furthermore, Great Sage!
It is like moths: they gather together when blown by the wind, but scatter as soon as the wind ceases.
Thus it is, Great Seer!
All realms of sentient beings are bound to one another by karma; performing the deeds of hell, they are born within hell and conjoin with those in hell.
Great Seer, you should know this:

In this way, sentient beings are bound to one another by their karma: those who practice the conduct of hungry ghosts are born among hungry ghosts and congregate with hungry ghosts; those who practice the conduct of animals are born among animals and congregate with animals; and those who practice the conduct of humans or devas are born among humans or devas and congregate with humans or devas.
The Great Sage spoke again:
“O All-Powerful One, All-Knowing One!
World-Honored One worthy of offerings!”
"Please explain this further for me: how can one know that a certain being has been born among humans?
From what place did they come together to be born here?
The Buddha said:

“Great Seer! If there are sentient beings who, having been born together in hell, are subsequently reborn among humans, they will give rise to malicious thoughts upon seeing one another and harbor mutual hatred.
Upon seeing each other, some will suffer headaches, some will discharge excrement, and some will lose control of their urine.”
Great Seer, you should know:
these are the signs of beings who have been gathered together in hell and are now being born among humans.
If there are such signs among humans, one should know that they have come from being gathered together in hell.
The Great Seer spoke again:
"O World-Illuminator, Omniscient One! Pray tell me further:
how may one know those who, having been in union with others among the animal realm, are reborn among humans? Furthermore, what are their marks?"
The Buddha said, “Great Seer!

If there are people who, having previously lived together in the animal realm, are now born among humans, they will give rise to anger upon seeing one another; they will seek out each other’s faults and shortcomings, constantly watching for opportunities to cause distress and confusion.”
Great Seer, you should know:
these are the signs of beings who were joined together among animals being born among humans.
If there are such signs among humans, one should know that they have come from being joined together among animals.
"Furthermore, Great Seer!

If a person has previously lived among the hungry ghosts (*preta*) and is reborn here among humans, they will delight in foul odors, have a greedy nature regarding food and drink, and be stingy and unwilling to give.
Those who come from dwelling together with hungry ghosts will feel envy upon seeing wealth and happiness, and long for the possessions of others."
Great Seer, you should know:
these are the signs of beings who were once gathered among the hungry ghosts and are now born among humans.
If there are those among humans with such signs, one should know that they have come from being gathered among the hungry ghosts.
"Furthermore, Great Seer!

If a person was previously in the human realm, having been joined with another in a different place and then again born as a human, then upon seeing one another, they will give rise to a mind of defilement."
"If there is one among human beings with such characteristics, they have originally come from a state of harmony among humans;
it should be known thus. That great seer asked:
"World-Honored One!"
“If a deva who has fallen from the heavenly realm is reborn among humans, what are his characteristics?
Furthermore, how can he be known?
The Buddha said:
"Great Seer! If a person was previously united with a celestial being and has been reborn among humans, they will look upon one another with joy and never tire of gazing.
If there is such a sign among humans, one should know that they have come from having been united with a celestial being in a previous life."
“Great Seer, you should know that such is the characteristic of the causal conditions for the aggregation of sentient beings.
At that time, the Great Seer named Jyotirarcis, having heard the Buddha’s teaching, felt great joy in his heart and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
If there are those who do not seek omniscience, all that such sentient beings do will be empty and yield no attainment.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the great seer Jyotirṣabha, saying:
"Regarding the subtle self within the bodies of sentient beings that you have asked about, Great Sage, you should listen:
if there were anyone who could conceptually apprehend a sentient being, they would then conceptually distinguish a subtle self within that sentient being."
Great Seer, you should know this:
it is like a person born blind who has no eyes; someone asks him, "What is white?"
"What do you think?
Can that person born blind, who has never seen form, describe such a kind of form?
The Great Sage replied:
"It cannot be said. The Buddha said, "So it is, so it is."
"O Great Sage!
That man born blind has never seen with his eyes, and therefore cannot speak of it.
I am likewise; I do not perceive the subtle internal self within sentient beings, and for this reason, I do not speak of it."
"Furthermore, O Great Seer!
The eye is not a sentient being;
likewise, it is not the ear, nor the nose, nor the tongue, nor the body, nor the mind that receives the designation 'sentient being'."
Furthermore, O Great Seer!

It is not by means of the five aggregates of clinging that the name "sentient being" is obtained; nor is it by means of the eighteen elements, the twelve bases, or the twelve links of dependent origination that the name "sentient being" is obtained.
Furthermore, Great Seer!
It is not through internal emptiness that the name "sentient being" is obtained, nor through external emptiness, nor through internal-and-external emptiness.
Great Seer, you should know this:
The mindfulness of the eye does not abide, changing and shifting without ceasing;
likewise, the mindfulness of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind all do not abide, changing and shifting without ceasing.
"So it is, Great Seer!
The five aggregates are likewise: they do not abide for even a single moment, changing and shifting without ceasing.
Thus it is, Great Seer!"
The thirty-six kinds of impure things do not abide in thought; they change and transform without ceasing.
Within such things as these, there is no name for a sentient being.
"Furthermore, O Great Seer!
The aggregation of material phenomena is conventionally designated as a "sentient being.
If one reflects upon and analytically examines it part by part, one finds no life-principle (*jīva*), no nourished person (*poṣa* or *pudgala*), nor any human (*manuṣya*) or youth (*mānava*).
"Great Seer, you should know this:
if there were sentient beings, the Tathāgata would not preach the Dharma of the Four Noble Truths;
if there were no sentient beings, that would be the Tathāgata."
"If one does not know the Dharma, it is like grasping through aggregation, like grasping through the mind.
At that time, the Great Seer Jyotirasa said:
"World-Honored One!"
"O World-Honored One! From this day forth, I, Prabhāketu, shall seek all-knowledge.

World-Honored One! Suppose one great kalpa were made a single day and night; suppose thirty such days were counted as a month; suppose twelve such months were counted as a year; and suppose years were counted in this manner until a kalpa was completed."
“World-Honored One!
I would rather remain forever in a pit of fire for such infinite eons.
Even if Mount Sumeru were as high and vast as the Akaniṣṭha Heaven, I would rather, for such infinite eons, fall from that mountain at every thought-moment, casting my body down to the ground.”
"Just as the fires at the end of an eon burn fiercely in five places, I would rather constantly roast myself with these same five fires throughout boundless eons.
World-Honored One!
I would rather endure such sufferings as these than ever abandon all-knowledge; I shall seek the causes and conditions for all-knowledge with diligence and never rest."
At that time, the various sages possessing the five supernormal powers all approached the World-Honored One; rising from their seats once more, they addressed the World-Honored One, saying:
"From this day forward, we seek anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and shall exert diligent effort according to our capacity."
At that time, after the World-Honored One had spoken thus to the seer, he emitted a ray of light from between his eyebrows; the name of this light was Vinipati.
Once this light had issued forth, it illuminated the ten directions universally; likewise, from the space between the eyebrows of all Buddhas in those ten directions, such radiance was also emitted.

By the power of the *Vini-vati* light, this great earth shook in six ways: that is, it quaked and quaked equally, trembled and trembled equally, surged and surged equally; it rose in the west and sank in the east, and rose in the south and sank in the north.
All the Buddhas, Tathāgatas of the ten directions, rained down flowers from above, scattering them over this assembly of Buddhas; the wondrous sounds of celestial drums were most delightful.
The Gandharva Kings performed the fivefold music as an offering to the Tathāgata, praising the World-Honored One, while winds blew celestial incense to perfume the Tathāgata.

The Bodhisattva, filled with joy, cast various necklaces into the air above the Tathāgata; he made offerings to the Tathāgata with flowers, incense, burning perfumes, exquisite garlands, ointments, scattered fragrances, various fine robes, banners, parasols, and silk streamers.
The devas rejoiced, raining down mandārava and mahāmandārava flowers from the midst of the sky.
The entire great assembly felt joy in their hearts and offered the exquisite robes they were wearing to the Tathāgata.

At that time, the Vini-vati light of the Tathāgata Śākyamuni here—shining upward as far as the celestial palaces of the Akaniṣṭha gods and downward as far as the Avīci Hell—having thus illuminated them, circled around the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, of the ten directions, and then returned to enter the crown of the World-Honored One’s head.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Tathāgata with these sublime verses:
“O Son of the Śākyas, like the morning sun, you radiate light throughout the ten directions.
This is not without cause; I pray that you will explain it to me.”
Seeing the Lord of Men display his majestic power, this assembly all gave rise to doubt;
yet some felt joy, their pure hearts full of longing.
Some joined their palms together, while others exclaimed, "Excellent!"
I only pray that the Tathāgata will speak, To sever the doubts of sentient beings.
Śakra, King of the Gods in the sky, And Brahmā, Lord of the World—
all in their hearts Give rise to joy, Praising his true merits.
"In the void of space, the various devas rain down all kinds of wondrous flowers;
there are many musical instruments that sound spontaneously without being struck.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Venerable Subhūti, saying:
“Subhūti, do you see the great seer Prabhāketu? Subhūti!”

In the future, this person shall attain Buddhahood in the world-system of Candraprabha, receiving the name Vipaśyin Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha; he will appear simultaneously as the final Tathāgata among the one thousand Tathāgatas of this Bhadrakalpa.

Subhūti! If there are sentient beings who hear the name of the Tathāgata Vipaśyin, they shall all receive his majestic power—just like a wish-fulfilling jewel, they shall obtain whatever they require.
Subhūti! Eighty-four thousand great ṛṣis, upon hearing this Dharma-gate, attained the stage of non-retrogression. Subhūti!

All of these shall attain the tenth stage within the Dharma of the World-Honored One Maitreya, and after three hundred kalpas, they shall be born in the world of the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Svayaṃprabha.

“Subhūti! Upon hearing this Dharma-gate, immeasurable bodhisattvas immediately attained the Śūraṅgama Samādhi, the Sound-Knowledge Samādhi, the Samādhi of Receiving the Supreme Position, the Illusion-like Samādhi, the Supreme Realm Samādhi, the Wisdom King Samādhi, the Ocean-Treasury Samādhi, the Earth-Treasury Samādhi, the Space-Treasury Samādhi, and the Samādhi of Attaining Radiance.”
Subhūti! There were as many devas as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River, all of whom attained the forbearance of the non-arising of dharmas;
and immeasurable bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās realized arhatship.

Subhūti! Gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and others, numbering as many as the sands of the Ganges River, have resolved their minds upon anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
“Subhūti! Seeing these causes and conditions, the Tathāgata emits this Vini-vati light that shines everywhere.
At that time, the World-Honored One smiled serenely, and from the root of his tongue, he extended it until it completely covered his face.

From within that tongue-root, immeasurable colors emerged—various colors such as blue, yellow, red, white, purple, and crystal-colored—and they pervaded immeasurable and boundless worlds; thereafter, they returned and entered the soles of the World-Honored One’s feet.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Akṣayamati rose from his seat, adjusted his robes to expose one shoulder, knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms toward the Buddha, and addressed him, saying:
"World-Honored One!
“If there is no cause or condition, the Tathāgata does not smile.
For what cause and condition, World-Honored One, do you smile now?
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva Akṣayamati, saying:
“Good son! For the benefit of those beings who lack faith, I have extended my tongue and smile; it is not that one who speaks falsely possesses such a tongue.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Akṣayamati addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
If a son of good family or a daughter of good family were to expound even a single verse of this Dharma-gate for others, how much merit would they obtain?”
The Buddha said, “Good son! Throughout the worlds of the ten directions,

within the entire range of the Buddha’s vision— the sphere of the Buddha-eye— whatever offerings and all manner of articles of pleasure exist for making offerings to all Buddhas, and even after those Buddhas have entered parinirvāṇa, whatever merit there is in constructing stūpas for them;”

Furthermore, if there is anyone who can explain even a single verse of this Dharma-gate of the phrases on the meaning of reality to others, they will obtain far more merit than the previous merit. "Good son!
If one conceives a pure mind toward those who expound this sublime Dharma-gate and praises them, saying, "Excellent!", such a person is praising all Buddhas;
furthermore, if there are those who can make offerings to them, it is no different from making offerings to us.
At that time, the World-Honored One surveyed the entire assembly.
Having surveyed them, he spoke these words:
"I now speak the truth."
"Noble son! In whatever place this Dharma-gate exists, that location shall be beheld by all Buddhas."
“Good son! This Dharma-gate is like medicine for sentient beings in the Jambudvīpa of future ages.

If there are those who can practice this Dharma-gate in three ways—whether by reading it, reciting it, or explaining it to others—that person will be no different from one who requested the turning of the Wheel of Dharma while the Buddha was in the world.”

“Good son! If one can transcribe such a Dharma-gate as this, it will not be difficult for that person to easily attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi; they shall be able to uphold and maintain all the treasuries of the Buddhas.”
“Good son! Those who travel upon evil paths do not even hear of such a Dharma-gate. Good son!”
If there are sentient beings who hear this Dharma-gate even once, after they have cast off their human bodies, they will be reborn in the pure worlds of the Buddhas.
O son of good family!
"If there are those who have made offerings to a thousand Buddhas and planted various roots of goodness, only then will this Dharma-gate pass through their ears. 'Good son!

If a good man or a good woman hears this Dharma-gate, and having heard it, gives rise to faith, receives and upholds it, reads and recites it, and is able to explain it to others—I say that for such a person, Bodhi is in the palm of their hand; I say that such a person will certainly obtain the five eyes, from this point forward their faculties will not be inferior, and at the time of the end of life they will not lose right mindfulness.'"

That person shall attain the Samādhi of the Assemblage of All Buddhas, the Samādhi of Vairocana’s Vigorous Display, the Samādhi of the Treasury of Dhāraṇīs, the Samādhi of the Jewel-Seal Topknot, the Samādhi of Bestowing Prophecy, the Samādhi of the World-Observing Seal, and the Samādhi of the Letterless Casket;

they shall attain the supreme dhāraṇī of all dharmas, the dhāraṇī that cuts off doubt, and the dhāraṇī of certainty regarding the ultimate truth, as well as immeasurable hundreds of thousands of such gateways to dhāraṇīs;
they shall attain the five supernormal powers, and according to their mental recollections, they will possess mastery over their rebirth.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Dharma Prince Mañjuśrī, saying: “Mañjuśrī!

You have already made offerings to many Buddha-World-Honored Ones; you are thus able to protect and keep this Dharma-gate in mind, and furthermore, you are able to expound it extensively for others in various places.”

Mañjuśrī! How many Buddhas have you served by making offerings to them, honoring them, attending upon them, and respecting and praising them? Mañjuśrī! What roots of goodness do you possess from all these acts?
What do you think? Do such roots of goodness have a limit,
or are they limitless?
"Can it be measured? Mañjuśrī replied,
"World-Honored One!"
"It is immeasurable. The Buddha said, "Mañjuśrī!"
If one can extensively expound such a Dharma-gate for others during this period of the five turbidities and chaos in this Sahā world, their merit shall surpass that of the former. Mañjuśrī!

If you were to provide only robes, food and drink, bedding and seats, and medicinal requisites for the sick to such Buddhas and Tathāgatas, yet did not explain this Dharma-gate to others, you would incur an offense against those Buddhas.
Mañjuśrī! If you have never made offerings to even a single Buddha, yet extensively expound such a Dharma-gate for others, then you have made offerings to all Tathāgatas.

When the World-Honored One had finished speaking, Mañjuśrī, the son of the Dharma King, the great seers such as Prabhāketu, and the entire assembly—including devas, humans, asuras, gandharvas, and others—having heard what the Buddha taught, rejoiced and praised him.
The Sūtra on the Supreme Dharma of the Ultimate Truth (Paramārthadharmavaiśeṣika-sūtra)
